scope: Qualified TableSpec scalar facet classification and authored projection under explicit consumer/input/obligation profiles, with retained native and ideal recovery

regression.scope: All core/core-ideals and five priority-system tests except Field, Nullability and Cardinality conformance gates, which run separately after evidence revalidation.

criteria.AC1: All priority regression tests pass, including native classification, explicit suite and authored projection tests with strict/report loss, unknown content and both recovery directions
criteria.AC2: Combined native entrypoint passes seven commands with pinned model/schema/generator and actual emitted GX value evidence
criteria.AC3: Combined Chromium entrypoint passes both directions and explicit suites against the public browser bundle, without host globals or external requests; type checks pass
criteria.AC4: Full five-priority-system refresh and Field/Nullability/Cardinality conformance gates pass; package describes import and export with qualified profiles

limits: Experimental core 0.5.0; this accepts the TableSpec binding only. PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Avro and Parquet facet bindings and the distinct facet admission/delivery gate remain required.

Declarations, raw/normalized generated schemas, baseline GX, explicit GX suites and ingest-cast profiles are distinct. This does not qualify whole-pipeline execution, write-blocking policy, arbitrary SQL/Delta lowering or general row conversion.

String length is qualified for well-formed Unicode scalar strings; byte encodings remain explicit losses. Suite integer widths must fit the native signed-32-bit carrier. Decimal enforcement depends on the selected consumer.
Unknown native and authored refinements remain retained. Missing facets do not inherit native defaults; exact-input narrowing/rounding remains a residual or strict refusal.
Facet projection does not imply composition with the earlier native nullability/cardinality bindings; those retain their qualified source versions and subsets.
Receipt verification establishes consistency with retained source/request and exact native target, not authenticity.
OWL, DDD lifecycle, physical encodings and default execution remain extension-owned; no native-equivalence graduation is claimed.
